## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people and the number of employed people—not everyone without a job. To be counted as unemployed, a person generally must have been without work during the reference week, available for work, and actively searching for a job during the four-week period ending with that week.

A person on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled may qualify without actively searching. They must still have been unemployed during the reference week and available for work, with temporary illness as an exception to the availability requirement.

By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings has not met the active-search requirement. That person would not qualify on that basis alone unless the temporary-layoff exception applies.

These conditions determine who is classified as unemployed and included alongside employed people in the rate’s denominator.
